assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib proved that inhibiting a driver kinase can control a cancer, creating the paradigm of targeted therapy and converting CML into a manageable disease. Clear, original, with enormous lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound development and kinase inhibitor program), Druker (preclinical selectivity and clinical trials) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) are the commonly cited trio. Rowley and others discovered the Philadelphia translocation and BCR-ABL, which is outside this candidate's credit, as is the Witte/Baltimore work.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of follow-up and confirmation; extremely mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views the story as incomplete without Rowley-type cytogenetic and oncogene discovery, and Lasker 2009 already honored the trio, which may be treated as a precedent rather than a barrier.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, creating a new class of living drugs. Conceptually original (redirecting T cells with synthetic receptors, co-stimulation design) and clinically decisive, with approved products worldwide.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (co-stimulated CAR design, preclinical principles), June (first clinical proof in CLL and translational program) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy, TIL and early gene-engineered T cells) are plausible. Eshhar and others who pioneered chimeric receptors are not in the credited list, so the story may be incomplete; I rely on my recollection here.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation across many centers and several approved products; long-term follow-up now shows cures in subsets. Solid-tumor and toxicity limitations remain, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Foundational chimeric-receptor work by individuals outside the credited names may complicate fair attribution.
Rosenberg's contribution is adjacent (adoptive cell transfer) rather than CAR design itself.
Limited efficacy in solid tumors and safety issues such as cytokine release and secondary malignancy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Microbial channelrhodopsins turned into tools to control defined cell types with millisecond precision transformed causal circuit neuroscience, including my own field of locomotor circuit dissection, and extended to cardiac and other physiology. It is a discovery-plus-tool story of broad lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterized channelrhodopsin function; Deisseroth led its use in neurons and behavior and the wider toolkit. Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck have real claims, so any three-person prize leaves out defensible contributors. I choose the names that best span discovery and neuronal application.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and used in thousands of labs; clinical translation (vision restoration) is emerging. Recognition is timely, although this is a method rather than a disease mechanism.
uncertainties: Credit is contested among six credited names, and I cannot resolve priority for neuronal expression.
Whether the committee treats enabling tools as sufficiently medicine-oriented.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defined GLP-1 as an incretin and glucagon-regulating hormone and led to durable drugs that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefit. A rare case of basic physiology becoming mass-impact medicine, with a clear conceptual chain from hormone biology to therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of GLP-1 secretion and action) and Drucker (proglucagon-derived peptides, intestinotrophic and metabolic actions, translational advocacy) are core. Knudsen is the key figure for long-acting analogues (liraglutide, semaglutide). Mojsov's contribution (identification of the active peptide GLP-1(7-37)) and the roles of other early workers such as Habener are matters of contested credit and constrain a three-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: Clinical outcomes are robust, replicated across large independent trials and years of real-world use; recognition would be timely, if anything late.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Mojsov, Habener-type early peptide work, Holst, Drucker and Knudsen is disputed and I cannot verify it independently.
Whether the committee prefers to honor physiology versus drug development, which would change the three names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanism-based antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, a therapy that changed the natural history of spinal muscular atrophy, a motor neuron disease. Strong example of RNA biology to disease-modifying treatment, with relevance to motor neuron disease broadly.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and the ISS-N1 target concept, with Bennett's group delivering the antisense chemistry and drug development. Other contributors (for example Hua and Adrian Krainer's collaborators, and gene discovery by Melki and Lefebvre) are outside the credited list or in a different candidate, so the prize could be criticised for omitting the SMN1 gene discovery.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long follow-up and multiple independent replications of benefit; a platform effect for oligonucleotide therapeutics. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: SMN1 gene discovery and other SMA therapies (gene therapy, risdiplam) complicate the narrative.
Allocation between academic mechanism and company drug development.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle vaccines demonstrated near-complete protection against persistent HPV infection and precancer, enabling cervical cancer prevention at population scale. Original and decisive prevention science with measurable reductions in disease.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity), Frazer (parallel VLP work and Gardasil development) form the usual set; Zhou's contribution to the early L1/L2 expression in Frazer's lab and Koutsky and company trial roles are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Population-level effectiveness data now show falling cervical cancer incidence; mature and independently confirmed. A prize in 2008 went to the HPV virus discovery, which may bear on how much overlap the committee sees.
uncertainties: Credit disputes between Frazer, Zhou and the NIH group are unresolved from the supplied record.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-term potentiation is the leading cellular model for synaptic plasticity underlying learning and memory, with the NMDA receptor mechanism giving molecular depth. Foundational and conceptually clear, though direct proof of its role in memory remains debated.
assessment.attribution: Bliss and Lømo reported LTP in 1973; Collingridge defined NMDA receptor dependence; Morris linked NMDA-dependent plasticity to spatial learning behavior. A three-person split necessarily omits one of these, and Morris's behavioral link is a strong competitor to Collingridge.
assessment.maturity: Replicated for fifty years across labs; mature, if somewhat late. Therapeutic impact is indirect, which may weigh against it in a medicine prize.
uncertainties: Causal link between LTP and memory is supported but not fully settled.
Choice between Collingridge and Morris for the third slot.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING axis defined how cytosolic DNA is sensed to trigger interferon responses, opening understanding of antiviral defense, autoimmunity, cancer immunity and aging inflammation. High originality and broad conceptual impact.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cGAMP second messenger, with Sun as a key first author of that discovery; Barber identified STING (as MITA/ERIS the work of Ishikawa and also Zhong and Shu with others). Credit for STING discovery is shared by several, which complicates a clean grouping.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many labs, and therapeutic programs (agonists, inhibitors) are still in clinical development, so clinical validation is not yet established. Possibly slightly early.
uncertainties: Priority for STING discovery is shared among Barber, Ishikawa, and groups not credited.
Whether a trainee should be co-recipient.
